J U D G M E N T / AWAR D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (North-West) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt.
LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act,
Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

entities.text: Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 2005-06 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/- per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/- per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar in possession of share in the land bearing Khasra no.41//6(4-16), 42//7 min(0- 04), 14min(2-06), 15(4-16), 17min(3-19) having 1/8th share of Sh. Rajinder Singh, 1/16th share of Sh. Ram Avtar, 1/16th share of Sh. Samunder Singh and 1/16th share of Ved Verk of total land admeasuring 16 bigha 1 biswa situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi (in short,
the said land).
LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 Rajinder Singh (805-06) vs Uoi (Rani Khera) on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142945989/
2 5.

entities.text: Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is stated that the award passed by the LAC is not accepted by the claimant and therefore the present reference petition is filed with a view to re-assess the market value of the land which has been arbitrarily assessed by the LAC without taking into account of fertility, potentiality,
surroundings and topography under acquisition.

6. It is stated that the land under acquisition is plain and levelled land and is situated in a belt which has not experienced any major earth quake, flood or any other natural calamity for the last more than 100 years and is best suited for all sorts of land uses like residential, commercial, industrial and agricultural etc.
7.
It is stated that the land under acquisition falls in the most fertile belt of Delhi and the claimant is cultivating the land and is growing three crops in a fasali year.

The whole of the land is having well developed irrigation system having canal and all crops including cereals, vegetable crops, oil yielding crops and sugar cane are cultivated by the claimant and income of the claimant per acre is more than Rs.2 Lacs per year.

It is further stated that in addition to this, the claimant is having milk yielding cattles which are fully feed by the land produce and almost all daily needs of claimant are fulfilled by the land under acquisition.
8.
It is stated that the land of the claimant acquired by the present acquisition is surrounded by residential as well as industrial area.

The area under acquisition is having metalled roads and is having very good LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Rajinder Singh & Ors. v.
Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 connectivity with other areas of Delhi.

entities.text:
Rajinder Singh & Ors. v.
Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The National Highway No.10 is just 1 KM away from the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera and railway line is just  km away.

9. It is stated that the LAC has great potentiality and it is fit for supporting high rise buildings and other residential infrastructure with a lesser investment if we compare the same with the development work carried out in South Delhi and East Delhi where the land was hilli tarrain and low line respectively which requires a huge amount for levelling and marketing the land useable for construction activities.
10. It is stated that the LAC has over looked while determining the market value of the land in question.
If all the factors are taken together for calculating the market value of the land under acquisition it shall be Rs.1 Crore per acre or at least Rs.2,000/- per sq. yards.

11. It is prayed that the petitioners by way of present petition are claiming market value of the said land @ Rs.2,000/- per square yard or Rs.1 Crore Per acre along with 30% solatium and additional amount @ 12% and further interest @9% and 15% per annum with effect from the date of the notification under Section 4 of the Act.

12. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/LAC and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the notification u/s 4 of LA Act was issued on 21.03.2003 and the declaration u/s 6 of LA Act was issued on LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Rajinder Singh &
Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 18.03.2003.

entities.text:
Rajinder Singh &
Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The petitioners are not entitled for compensation in respect of construction of structure, which is placed without the sanction of law and in terms of Rajinder Singh (805-06) vs Uoi (Rani Khera) on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142945989/
3 section 4 notification there were no structure, tree, well on the said land.
The said land is not surrounded by any developed or undeveloped colony and can be used for agricultural purposes only.
The ld. LAC categorised the land into two categories on the basis of survey carried out as per the fertility and user of land.

13. It is submitted that the ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land by adopting the indicative price fixed by the government of NCT of Delhi @ Rs. 15,70,000 per acre for for the year 2001 - 2002 which is applicable with effect from 01.04.2001.
The ld. LAC adopted the indicative price fixed by the Government of NCT of Delhi of land falling in "Block A".

As far as the land having ghadda upto 2-3 feet, the ld. LAC has deducted Rs. 1,70,000 per acre from the market value of "Block A" category land, therefore, after deduction the value comes to Rs. 12,30,000 per acre, and as such the market value of the said land was assessed as per the rate prevailing during the corresponding period for different categories of land besides other statutory benefits.
It is submitted that the ld. LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view the aspects enumerated under Section 23 and 24 of the Act.
All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioners are misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.
LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 12 14.

entities.text: Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award relating to village Rani Khera had taken into consideration the market value of the said land on the basis of the said sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

15. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by the ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.
16. The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore, is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.
As per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award, reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days
therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.

It is stated that DDA is not liable to pay compensation as the said land has not been taken over by the DDA either due to stay by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi or has been handed over to DDA and subsequently taken back by land and building Department from DDA and handed over to DSIDC.

LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 12 Rajinder Singh (805-06) vs Uoi (Rani Khera) on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142945989/

entities.text: Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is stated that the possession of the said land has been handed over to DDA on 15.03.2007 and after taking the possession, the same has been transferred to RPD-VII.

The Award passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioners are not entitled for grant of any enhanced compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioners in reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioners is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioners is liable to be dismissed with cost.

18. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 03.09.2013: -
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount ?
2. Relief.
19.
Matter was listed for recording of petitioner's evidence.

To prove the case, Sh. Ravinder Dabas,
advocate of petitioner has been examined as PW-1 and tendered evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW-1/A on behalf of petitioner no.1, 2 and 4.

He has adopted the leading case titled as Mukhtiyar Singh Vs. UOI & Ors. Vide LAC No.390/2016 and close PE.
20.

entities.text: Mukhtiyar Singh Vs. UOI & Ors. Vide LAC No.390/2016
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In order to prove the case, Sh. Samunder Singh has been examined as P3W1 and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.P3W1/A LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 8 of 12 and adopted the leading case titled as Mukhtiyar Singh Vs. UOI & Ors. vide LAC No.390/2016 and close PE.
21.

entities.text: Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mukhtiyar Singh Vs. UOI & Ors. vide LAC No.390/2016
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Vide order dated 21.12.2021, Ld. proxy counsel for DDA has tendered the copy of award as Ex.R2 and relied upon the evidences and cross examination done in leading case Mukhtiyar Singh Vs. UOI in LAC No.390/16 and close RE.
22.
Ld. Counsel for the petitioners as well as ld.
Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 390 of 2016 Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera.

entities.text: Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
23. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue-wise findings and determination are as under : -
WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED TO ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF SO, TO WHAT AMOUNT ?
Rajinder Singh (805-06) vs Uoi (Rani Khera) on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142945989/
5 24.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no.
9 of 12 our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
25.

entities.text: Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove its case, the petitioners, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioners have argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
26. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

27. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

28. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 12 2005-06 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/- per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/- per acre has been given.

entities.text: Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/- per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/- per acre.
29. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
RELIEF 30.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:-

(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @ Rs.19,73,583/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 31.

(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
LAC no. 440 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Rajinder Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 31.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
